## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Fix the Critical finding before merge: `refresh_fingerprints` replaces fingerprints for tracked files that have been edited by hand, so `verify` no longer detects those edits.

## Changes
The pull request adds `refresh_fingerprints` and `register_new_files` to `app/integrity.py`. Both write fingerprints for the given names into the JSON manifest. It also adds `tests/test_integrity.py` to cover both helpers.

## Critical
- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Skip names already in the manifest when refreshing — If you call `refresh_fingerprints(root, manifest, ["tracked.txt", "new.txt"])` after `tracked.txt` was edited by hand, it overwrites the stored digest with the digest of the edited file. `verify` then returns True. The test at `tests/test_integrity.py:12` uses an unchanged `tracked.txt`, so it cannot catch this overwrite. — When someone refreshes after adding files and includes a tracked name, tampering goes undetected; the PR body says existing fingerprints are there to catch exactly this. — Fix: Add the `if name not in entries` guard that `register_new_files` uses at app/integrity.py:24, then extend `test_refresh_registers_new_files_and_keeps_unchanged_entries` so it edits `tracked.txt` before the refresh.
